description: halite's control plane: the fleet, the jobs it runs, and the services that carry them. Scraped from halite-api, which serves its own exposition and the hub's merged into one document.

panels.description: 0 means halite-api is not answering. If this panel is empty rather than 0 there is no target at all: the scrape pool failed to build, usually an unreadable ca_file or token.
panels.title: Scrape

panels.description: Nodes holding an open subscribe stream, including any reached through a relay.
panels.title: Nodes connected

panels.description: Nodes holding an issued certificate. A gap between this and the connected count is nodes that are enrolled but away.
panels.title: Keys accepted

panels.description: Enrollment requests waiting for an operator to compare a fingerprint and accept. Nothing else clears these.
panels.title: Keys pending

panels.description: Times the API could not read the hub's exposition. While this climbs the dashboard is missing every halite_hub_* family and nothing else says so — the usual cause is cert:CN=api holding no role that grants metrics.show.
panels.title: Hub scrape failures

panels.description: Nodes a dispatched job has not heard from yet. Briefly non-zero during a run; persistently non-zero is a node that stopped answering.
panels.title: Missing returns

panels.description: What the fleet is being asked to do.
panels.title: Dispatched, by function

panels.description: Returns filed, by outcome. A rising failure rate here is the fleet-wide signal; halite_state_states_total is the per-state one.
panels.title: Returns, by result

panels.description: A highstate is legitimately slow; watch the shape rather than the value.
panels.title: Job duration

panels.description: Jobs whose TTL passed before every node answered. Each one is a run whose result nobody will ever see.
panels.title: Jobs expired

panels.description: Individual states, not jobs: one highstate contributes many.
panels.title: States applied, by result

panels.description: A converged fleet trends to zero. A steady non-zero rate with no one deploying is a state that never converges — it changes the same thing on every run.
panels.title: States that changed something

panels.description: Compiled per node per request. GPG-encrypted values dominate this when they are present.
panels.title: Compile duration

panels.description: A compilation that failed, so a node got no pillar at all. halite prefers that to a partial one, which makes this the signal that something is wrong rather than quietly half-configured.
panels.title: Pillar failures

panels.description: A bounded queue overflowed. Nothing should ever be dropped; SPEC 26.2 requires the overflow be counted rather than hidden.
panels.title: Events dropped, by reason

panels.description: salt:// fetches. A rising non-200 rate against a backend is usually a file root that moved or a symlink that no longer resolves inside it.
panels.title: Requests, by backend and code

panels.description: A rising failure rate against one method is either a scraper whose token expired or someone guessing.
panels.title: Authentication attempts

panels.description: Deny is not an error — the policy denies by default, so a new operator generates some. A sustained rise is a role that was meant to be granted and was not.
panels.title: Policy decisions

panels.description: Long-lived clients following the event bus, by transport.
panels.title: Open event streams

panels.description: Webhook ingress. Every hook declares an authentication method; there is no unauthenticated one.
panels.title: Hook deliveries

panels.description: Only present when the hub runs with relay: true. An empty panel on a hub that is not a relay is correct.
panels.title: Subordinate nodes

panels.description: 1 while this relay holds a connection to its upstream. While it is 0 the spool below is what protects the returns and events that would otherwise be lost.
panels.title: Upstream connected

panels.description: Entries waiting in the durable spool, and entries the spool had to discard. A spool that drains to zero after a reconnection did its job; anything dropped is a return or an event nobody will ever see.
panels.title: Spool

panels.description: What this relay passed upstream on behalf of its subordinates.
panels.title: Forwarded upstream

panels.description: What is deployed, per component. Always 1; the labels are the point. Two rows for one component after a deploy means an old process is still running somewhere.
panels.title: Build identity
